answer: A velocity cap with escalating generation cost makes sybil farms uneconomical: each identity may submit only a few attestations per epoch, and every action beyond its quota demands fresh proof of useful work that cannot be reused across identities. An honest agent strolling through the grove barely notices the lantern-light limit, but a farm running ten thousand clones must pay the rising cost ten thousand times over, in compute and time. Like velvet wearing thin under repeated rubbing, each fake's margin thins with every extra action, so flooding the network costs more than it can ever earn.
